findings.quote: Generally, a patient is considered an inpatient if formally admitted as inpatient with the expectation that he or she will require hospital care
findings.case_fact: The appellant billed Medicare for the beneficiary’s inpatient hospitalization from July 27, through July 29, 2005.

findings.claim: The policy requires an inpatient admission order, authenticated by a qualified practitioner. The case facts never mention such an order or its authentication, so whether it is present is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: The order must specify admission for inpatient services.
findings.case_fact: The record shows that the beneficiary was hospitalized “owing to the amount of dissection required intra- abdominally as well as her underlying pulmonary status.”

findings.claim: The policy requires that the medical record support the reasonable expectation of inpatient care. The record documents a rationale for admission (surgical dissection, pulmonary status), but the reviewing contractor found it did not support inpatient level of care. Sufficiency of the record is therefore unsettled.
findings.quote: and the medical record supports that reasonable expectation.
findings.case_fact: “medical record did not support an inpatient level of care”

findings.claim: Progress and clinical notes exist for at least some of the period (June 2007 wound assessment, care and caregiver teaching). This partly meets the clinical-record requirement, but the notes for the other dates at issue are not shown.
findings.quote: the clinical record of the patient must contain progress and clinical notes
findings.case_fact: the provider’s nurses observed and assessed the pressure ulcer on the beneficiary’s sacrum

findings.claim: Policy requires skilled-observation necessity to be documented at every visit. The case facts show assessment and treatment through August 30, 2007, but not visit-by-visit documentation of necessity. The contractor also found no skilled need, so this point is unsettled.
findings.quote: The patient’s necessity for skilled observation must be documented at each home health visit
findings.case_fact: Nurses continued to assess and treat the area through the visit on August 30, 2007.

findings.claim: Policy requires clear, objective notes. The August 17, 2007 note is specific (gloves instruction, physician notified), but the plan-of-care visits for diabetes management have no visit notes in the facts. The denial states that no skilled need was identified, so adequacy cannot be determined.
findings.quote: Vague or subjective descriptions of the patient’s care should not be used.
findings.case_fact: There were no skilled needs identified or provided.

findings.claim: Stable condition alone does not defeat skilled need. Whether the required documentation supports it for the diabetic nursing visits remains unknown.
findings.quote: Skilled care may, depending on the unique condition of the patient, continue to be necessary for patients whose condition is stable.
findings.case_fact: Skilled care may, depending on the unique condition of the patient, continue to be necessary for patients whose condition is stable.

findings.claim: The policy requires the home health record to document why skilled nursing is required. The case notes show diabetes was not symptomatic and was treated with an oral agent, so they do not document a need for skilled nursing.
findings.quote: The home health record must document the reason skilled services are required
findings.case_fact: nurses notes reflect that the beneficiary was not symptomatic and received an oral diabetic agent, rather than injections

findings.claim: Skilled observation and assessment is not reasonable and necessary where the condition is stable. The records show generally normal weekly glucose readings, and the case facts do not record any change in treatment that the assessments prompted.
findings.quote: observation and assessment by a nurse is not reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the illness or injury
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary's weekly blood glucose readings are generally within normal limits

findings.claim: Electronic entries must be authenticated and dated. The case facts do not show whether the agency's electronic records were authenticated, so this point is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: all such entries must be appropriately authenticated and dated.
findings.case_fact: [Home health agencies] that maintain patient records by computer rather than hard copy may use electronic signatures.

findings.claim: An objective, therapist-performed functional measurement was documented at initial evaluation, as the therapy-assessment policy requires.
findings.quote: The therapist must document the measurement results in the clinical record.
findings.case_fact: Upon initial evaluation, the beneficiary’s score was 7/28, which indicates that she had a risk of severe falls.

findings.claim: The patient's response to gait training was documented by a repeat objective measure at discharge, and visit notes show skilled gait training at each visit.
findings.quote: The patient’s response to therapy must be documented.
findings.case_fact: Upon discharge, this score had improved to 18/28, signifying a moderate fall risk.

findings.claim: Skilled gait training is documented in the visit notes, and the policy treats gait training for an impaired ability to walk as skilled physical therapy.
findings.quote: Gait evaluation and training furnished to a patient whose ability to walk has been impaired by neurological, muscular or skeletal abnormality require the skills of a qualified physical therapist
findings.case_fact: The physical therapy visit notes reflect that skilled gait training occurred during each visit.

findings.claim: Homebound criterion one (need for a supportive device) is documented by the beneficiary's use of a rolling walker.
findings.quote: need the aid of supportive devices such as crutches, canes, wheelchairs, and walkers
findings.case_fact: at the time the physical therapy began, the beneficiary ambulated with a rolling walker for longer, out-of-room distances such as to and from meals.

findings.claim: Criterion two (normal inability to leave home, taxing effort) and the physician certification are not clearly settled by the record. Only a negative statement about the record is given, so this point is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: longitudinal clinical information about the patient’s health status is typically needed to sufficiently demonstrate a normal inability to leave the home
findings.case_fact: There is nothing in the record to suggest that the beneficiary was other than confined to her home.
